problems.stem: You add a screenshot of your two-factor setup to your digital citizenship portfolio. What turns it into usable evidence?
options: Leaving it as just the image, since it speaks for itself.
Adding a caption: "Enabled 2FA on my school email to protect my account; shows the account safety skill from this module."
Adding ten more screenshots so the portfolio looks full.
problems.explanation: Evidence needs context: what it is, which skill it demonstrates, and what you decided. A bare screenshot leaves the reviewer guessing.

problems.stem: Your module has four learning targets. Which portfolio is the strongest evidence of digital citizenship?
options: Twenty loosely related screenshots with no labels.
Four items, each captioned and mapped to one learning target, with a short note on what you decided or revised.
One long reflection essay with no artifacts attached.
The single most visually polished item, repeated in three formats.
problems.explanation: A few relevant items that each map to a target show competence better than a large pile of unlabeled files.

problems.stem: You ask AI to write your portfolio reflection. It produces a polished paragraph claiming you "mastered data privacy." Your portfolio has no privacy artifact. What is the responsible move?
options: Submit the AI reflection; it sounds confident.
Either attach a real privacy artifact that supports the claim or revise the reflection to match what you actually did, then disclose the AI help.
Keep the claim and hope the reviewer does not check.
Delete all reflections so no claims need evidence.
problems.explanation: Every skill claim must be backed by an artifact. AI polish cannot substitute for evidence, and AI use should be disclosed.

problems.stem: Your portfolio shows only the final, polished resume. A reviewer wants to see growth. What single addition best demonstrates your digital citizenship process?
options: A nicer font on the final resume.
A short before/after note: the original duty-only bullet, the revised result-based bullet, and one line on why you changed it.
A second copy of the final resume.
A statement that you worked hard on it.
problems.explanation: A before/after with a reason shows the reasoning behind the work, which is what process evidence requires; a polished final file alone does not.
